reason: Checked against tools/register_44b6_dorado.py (header), research/wf_ideas_v2/r2_critic.notes.md l.15-20, experiments/coordhead_retrain/out_full_Q.log l.55-112, CONTEXT.md l.1281-1290, and royerlab/ultrack_supplementary configuration/sparse_zebrafish (README, config.toml, main.sh, segment.sh via raw.githubusercontent). (1) The premise that the annotations follow Ultrack's convention is weaker than stated. The '84 %' in the idea means 84 % of GT nodes have a dorado Ultrack point within 2.5 um after a mean-shift-refined translation. It does not mean they coincide exactly. The residual median is 1.29 um. If GT were proofread Ultrack centroids, the residual would be about 0.3-0.5 um (integer rounding plus registration). So 44b6 GT are not copies of Ultrack's output, and 6bba is not in dorado at all. (2) The positive control already fails on data we have. On 44b6, GT->Ultrack is median 1.29 um (1.23 um even after removing the 0.4 um registration error in quadrature), with a <4 um share of 0.917. Our unheaded final nodes reach 0.927 on that share. The public head on 44b6 pre-ILP peaks is median 1.107 um / mean 1.296 um (out_full_Q.log emb_6bba_to_44b6), versus none at 1.675/1.499. So Ultrack's own points on the very recording they come from are about 10-15 % WORSE than the public head in median and no better in the tail. The samples differ (25 interior clips vs 71 clips), but the gap is larger than that mismatch would explain. (3) The score is driven by the tail, not the median. The 7 um re-match counts move by <= 50 of 112k for every head. The x138 relink and readmit gates are also 7 um. The v2 snap test moved the median 1.42 -> 1.22 but worsened the tail (<4 um 0.927 -> 0.908), which is the scored direction. A 2 um gate limits that damage, but it also limits the gain. (4) The swap-zone upside (GT->Ultrack 2.4 vs GT->pred 3.7 um) comes from Ultrack having +44 % more points (segmentation density). It does not come from better centroids of the same object. A centroid of the basin that contains our peak, gated at 2 um, cannot move a node toward a different nucleus, so the b_swap oracle (+0.03-0.046) is out of reach for this mechanism. (5) Value arithmetic. Of the head's +0.007 public gain on x138, ~+0.0026 is node multiplier and ~+0.0044 is a ~5-6 % cut in random error (v_detector-retrain_coordhead-v2-embryo-robust_value.json), i.e. ~+0.0007 per 1 %. Beating the public head by +0.002 needs a further >= 3 % sigma cut on an UNSEEN embryo. The only direct measurement (44b6, the most favourable case) points the other way. A 0.5/0.5 blend could cut uncorrelated error, but two things cap it: the GT noise both localisers share (integer-voxel z rounding, uniform +-0.81 um) and errors that are correlated because both are image-driven. Guess: 0-3 %, i.e. 0..+0.002. (6) Transfer. The 6bba 'none' z bias of +0.82 um is exactly 0.50 z-voxel (1.625/2). That looks like a rounding or voxel-origin convention that differs between embryos, a constant offset that Ultrack centroids would not reproduce and that the score barely rewards anyway. The hidden embryos' annotation pipeline is unknown. Even if it was Ultrack-proofread, the hosts may have used a newer model than the public unet-simview. The UNet preprocessing (normalisation, scale) is not in the supplementary repo: segment.sh reads precomputed detection/edge layers. And a one-level 'basin' is not the ILP-selected Ultrack segment. (7) Node-multiplier drift of +-0.001..0.003 from changed positions in the post-ILP stages (the head moved final nodes by -2.9 %), plus LB noise of 0.003, means one probe cannot resolve a central ~0 effect. The realistic public gain is below +0.002, so the idea fails the lens.
fix_if_any: Replace Step 1 with a zero-install, zero-GPU pre-kill on data the team already has, run before anyone installs ultrack. Friend C or friend A CPU, ~30-60 min: on the 63 reliably placed 44b6 clips (data_external/dorado/kaggle44b6_in_dorado.json + tracks.npz), compute per GT node the distance to (a) the nearest registered dorado Ultrack point, (b) our pre-ILP peak + public head shift (from the coordhead captures), and (c) the 0.5/0.5 blend of (a) and (b) where (a) lies within 2 um of the peak. Report offset-invariant numbers: per-video mean error subtracted, the <2.5/<4 um shares, and the 7 um re-match count, in the style of train_coordhead. KILL if (a) is not <= 0.95 x (b) in offset-invariant sigma AND at least equal in the <4 um share on 44b6. 44b6 is the most favourable case possible (same recording as the Ultrack tracks), so a failure there closes the line without touching 6bba. Only if it passes: run unet-simview on 6bba clips with the preprocessing confirmed from the ultrack repo's own predict code (not guessed), use the same offset-invariant gate, and ship at most as a passenger in a final with node counts within +-0.5 % of the base on every dummy movie, never as a stand-alone probe. Even repaired, expected value ~0..+0.002 public / private.
